reviews.pros:
Company culture is good.
Policies are good such as employee benefits, leaves.
reviews.cons:
Job security: Dell recently layed off more than 12000 employees and may cut down more head count so it's job security is a major issue.
Salary: Salary is little below market standards.
Appraisal/promotion : Once you reach to principal engineer position, promotion seems like an alien concept because 1 in around 30-40 principal engineer gets promoted to Sr principal level that too after ATLEAST after 10-12 years working as a principal engineer.
Skill development/Learning : NO Scope whatsoever for new learning. Most of people who left there jobs recently were due to lack of opportunities to learn new skills and were bored/tired of working on the same things for years.
So if you have a hunger to learn new things, Dell is certainly NOT a place for you.
Work satisfaction: As mentioned above there is no scope for new skill development and learning, people get sick of working on the same things and in turn are not satisfied with their work.

reviews.pros: I appreciate the friendly atmosphere and the camaraderie among colleagues at Dell. The team dynamic fosters a supportive environment where collaboration thrives. While the company culture may be average, the relationships I've built with my coworkers have made my experience enjoyable. Having friendly colleagues makes the workday more enjoyable and creates a sense of belonging within the team.
reviews.cons: I have several concerns about working at Dell. The poor work-life balance, with expectations to work late hours and weekends without compensation, is particularly challenging. Additionally, the management tends to be retaliative and blame-shifting, which creates a punitive atmosphere. The compensation and benefits are below industry standards, with annual merit increases falling short of the inflation rate. The work culture can be toxic, pressuring employees to overwork. Remote workers face an unfriendly culture, often being forced to adopt a hybrid model and treated as second-class employees. Long, unproductive meetings further reduce overall productivity, and there are limited opportunities for career growth and advancement.

benefits.name: Physical Well-being
benefits.details: We care about our team members — personally and professionally — and are committed to ensuring they have what they need to live life to the fullest. We empower team members to take charge of their health and well-being through innovative and engaging programs to stay healthy and focus on what matters most.

benefits.name: Mental and Emotional Health and Well-being
benefits.details: We believe emotional health directly affects physical health. Confidential, professional counseling through our Employee Assistance Program (EAP) is one of many resources we offer to support emotional and mental well-being. We also have resources through our global wellness platform to help ease stress, build resilience, create connections and develop simple, healthy habits.

benefits.name: Financial Well-being
benefits.details: Financial wellness is essential to overall health and well-being. We offer access to programs that help team members find financial balance — supporting their short and long-term financial goals.

benefits.name: Flexibility
benefits.details: Time away is important and our time away programs ensure team members can take the time needed for optimal physical and mental wellness.
